stories.headline: BJP slams Congress over 'vandalism' at Meta offices, calls it 'party of goons'
stories.bodyText:
New Delhi: The BJP on Saturday said the Congress was a "party of goons" that promoted vandalism after alleged vandalism at Meta offices by Indian Youth Congress workers.
Posting a video on X, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari alleged that Indian Youth Congress workers not only vandalised and destroyed Meta's office in Hyderabad but also flaunted the incident on social media.
"Congress is a party of goons! Goons of Indian Youth Congress not only vandalised and destroyed Meta's office in Hyderabad, they are also are flaunting it on social media," he said.
Congress is a party of goons!
Goons of Indian Youth Congress are not only vandalised and destroyed Meta's office in Hyderabad, & also are flaunting it on social media!
Recall how they insulted India at World AI Summit by barging naked at the Summit!
He also recalled the protest by Youth Congress workers at the India AI Impact Summit in the national capital, alleging that they had "insulted" India by barging into the event and staging a shirtless protest.

stories.headline: PM, HM still searching for ‘supertainted’ two-thirds majority for delimitation bill: Congress
stories.bodyText:
PM, HM still searching for ‘supertainted’ two-thirds majority for delimitation bill: Congress
Jairam Ramesh said it is in the nation's interest to let the current Lok Sabha strength and state-wise configuration continue with one-third reservation for women implemented till the Viksit Bharat objective is achieved.
Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh
Credit: PTI
New Delhi: The Congress on Saturday said that 100 days have passed since the Monsoon session of Parliament was adjourned sine die, but Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah are still in search of a "supertainted" two-thirds majority in Lok Sabha to get the delimitation bill passed.
Congress General Secretary Jairam Ramesh said it is in the nation's interest to let the current Lok Sabha strength and state-wise configuration continue with one-third reservation for women implemented till the Viksit Bharat objective is achieved.
"Today is the 100th day since the 2026 Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die and has not been prorogued.
"The PM-HM jodi is still in search of a supertainted two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha to get the Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation passed," he said in a post on X.
The Congress leader said that nobody knows what the new Bill will contain since the old Bill was defeated “resoundingly” on April 17.
He said no new specific proposals have been discussed with any political party “in a serious and structured manner”, and added that an all-party meeting has not been called, “despite four letters to the Modi from Mallikarjun Kharge”.
Today is the 100th day since the 2026 Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die and has not been prorogued.
The PM-HM jodi is still in search of a supertainted two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha to get the Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation passed.…
"There are far more serious and pressing economic, political, social, military and foreign policy challenges that await and demand attention. Far-reaching and comprehensive Delimitation can wait. Indira Gandhi put it off for 25 years in 1976. In 2001, Atal Bihari Vajpayee put it off for a further twenty-five years, that is, till the results of the first census after 2026 are published. They were wise and nationalist PMs," Ramesh said in his post.
He recalled that the Prime Minister expressed grave concerns about the state of the economy at the FICCI conclave on November 19.
"He seems to be in a very disturbed state of mind, as indeed he should be. Debate and discussions on delimitation require cool heads unburdened by tensions of the type that are preoccupying the PM. Extensive consultations with various stakeholders are also needed.
"Under the circumstances, it is in the nation's interest to let the current Lok Sabha strength and state-wise configuration continue with one-third reservation for women implemented. This arrangement should then remain frozen till the much-trumpeted Viksit Bharat objective is achieved. It will be a fitting tribute to it since the consequences of a fundamentally new delimitation can best be managed in an environment when Viksit Bharat has become a reality," the Congress leader said.

stories.headline: At least 11 dead after consuming spurious liquor, over 300 hospitalised
stories.deck: Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications
stories.bodyText:
At least 11 people have died since November 18 in incidents linked to consumption of spurious alcohol in Manipur's Chandel district, while more than 300 others have been hospitalised.
The patients are mostly from Chakpikarong and surrounding areas and have been hospitalised across multiple healthcare facilities in Imphal, including JNIMS, RIMS, Shija and Babina Hospital.
Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited Shija Hospital and Babina Hospital on Friday afternoon (November 20, 2026) to assess the situation and meet patients undergoing treatment.
In a social media post, Mr. Singh said, "Visited Shija Hospital at Lamphelpat, and Babina Hospital at Sajiwa, today [on Friday] to enquire about the health condition of the persons undergoing treatment after consuming spurious liquor from Chakpikarong area in Chandel District."
"Over 140 patients were admitted to Shija Hospital and over 41 patients at Babina Hospital. The death toll has touched 11 during the last 48 hours. The patients are undergoing medical evaluation and treatment under the close supervision of the doctors," he said.
"A medical team, led by a Specialist in General Medicine, along with essential medicines, has left for Chandel District to strengthen on-ground treatment and response", he said adding, "The government will conduct an enquiry and the culprits will be punished."
Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan .K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications.
"Some patients are also undergoing hemodialysis", he added.
A JNIMS doctor said, "Many of the hospitalised include individuals who had consumed local liquor and had come to the hospital due to fear."
Shija Hospitals also informed that "over 312 patients [have been] attended [to] till now at Shija Hospitals due to methanol poisoning."
Preliminary reports suggest that the suspected contaminated alcohol was purchased from Sugnu in Kakching district.
Chandel constituency MLA S.S. Olish said arrangements are being made to bring more patients up to Imphal and has requested the chief minister to look into the situation.
She said, "I have spoken personally to CM Yumnam Khemchand, and requested him to look into the situation affecting Chandel. He agreed willingly and has visited the patients at Shija Hospitals and will visit Babina later."
"Moreover, party workers, especially in Chakpikarong, are working constantly, arranging vehicles to bring patients up to Imphal", she added.

stories.headline: From acid attacks to pellet wounds: Delhi-NCR dogs fight back for a second chance at life
stories.deck: Rescued after brutal acts of animal cruelty, four dogs are rebuilding their lives with an animal volunteer’s help. Their journeys of recovery also expose gaps in police investigations and the struggle to hold perpetrators accountable
stories.bodyText:
At a residence in south Delhi, a golden-furred dog keeps the household on its toes. With his bright coat and features resembling a Golden Retriever, Veer is now almost indistinguishable from any other happy, playful dog. But beneath his cheerful demeanour lies a painful past. An acid attack had left his face so severely damaged that veterinarians initially recommended euthanasia. A rare facial reconstruction surgery, however, gave him another chance at life.
Veer, now around four years old, was rescued from Ashok Nagar in August 2025 after animal rescue volunteer Priya Chopra received an emergency call around 2 a.m. The chemical had destroyed much of his facial tissue; his nose was hanging, one eye was shut and maggots had infested his wounds. He was in extreme pain, suffered seizures and repeatedly banged into walls. He initially had to be syringe-fed, Ms Chopra recalls.
She decided against giving up on him. At a private veterinary hospital in East of Kailash, doctors explored the possibility of reconstructing his face using tissue from his neck and thigh. The six-hour surgery involved nearly 200 stitches, followed by two months of hospitalisation. The treatment cost around ₹4 lakh in hospital expenses alone.
More than a year later, Veer has regained much of his ability to see, eat and move around, although he continues to live with some limitations. After struggling to adjust in three different places, he has finally found a home with Ms. Chopra in south Delhi.
But while Veer survived the attack, his case could not even make it to an FIR. The absence of CCTV footage to establish evidence was among the reasons, according to animal activists.
His is one of several cases that underline the brutality inflicted on community dogs across Delhi-NCR, even as animal cruelty receives greater visibility through social media and official crime statistics.
For the first time, the National Crime Records Bureau included offences under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act in its Crime in India 2024 report, recording 9,039 cases across the country. Delhi accounted for 35 cases. While the inclusion marks an important step towards recognising such offences, animal welfare volunteers say the numbers capture only reported cases, leaving the actual scale of cruelty difficult to establish.
In September 2026, an ambulance driver passing through Shahdara was stopped by locals, who told him that a resident had thrown boiling water on a 10-year-old street dog, later named Rudra, reportedly because it regularly sat on the person’s staircase. The driver took the injured dog to a hospital.
Rudra was in septic shock and barely responded to his surroundings. He remained hospitalised for nearly a month, undergoing intensive treatment for severe burns and septicaemia.
Shaurya, a two-year-old dog from Meerut’s Khirwa Jalalpur village, still carries the scars of an attack with a pellet gun.
On June 13, 2026, he was shot at close range. Radiographic scans revealed more than 200 lead pellets embedded across his skull, muzzle, eye and jaw. Around 150 pellets were surgically removed from his face and head, but several remain lodged in his body. He has permanently lost his vision, and his injured eye had to be stitched up.
Unlike Veer and Rudra’s cases, Shaurya’s attack resulted in a police case. An FIR was registered at Sardhana police station in Meerut on June 15 under Sections 3 and 11 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act and Section 325 (punishment for killing, poisoning, maiming or rendering an animal useless) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The chargesheet, however, is yet to be filed.
Closer to home, Neemo, now around five years old, was rescued after a juvenile allegedly smashed his face with a brick on a foot overbridge near the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Delhi. The dog was left bleeding and terrified. According to Ms. Chopra, the juvenile had allegedly attacked animals before as well, including a cow. Following treatment, Neemo recovered and returned to the area he once called home.
Animal activists lodged a complaint in the matter. However, no case was registered after a ‘disability certificate’ indicating that the juvenile had a mental disability was produced. Given the alleged repeated attacks on animals, activists are now seeking counselling for him.
While awareness and social media have significantly increased the reporting of animal cruelty, ensuring that cases reach their logical conclusion remains a challenge, Ms Chopra said. She alleged that police are often reluctant to register FIRs and that crimes against animals are not treated with the seriousness they deserve. In other cases, the absence of CCTV footage, witnesses and other evidence can prevent even horrific attacks from being formally registered. Even when FIRs are filed, accused persons may secure bail, with cases often failing to reach a conclusion, she added.

stories.headline: A perfect brew, a perfect blend: Rahul and Padikkal's coffee camaraderie
stories.deck: Devdutt Padikkal and KL Rahul share more than a batting partnership. A coffee obsession that began during India's 2024-25 Australia tour has taken over the dressing room, with players carrying their own brewing equipment on tours. At Wellington, the duo's 165-run stand showcased their understanding, patience composure, and blending cricketing chemistry with a shared love for the perfect brew.
stories.bodyText:
Wellington: The perfect blend for Devdutt Padikkal and 
KL Rahul
 isn't just at the crease. Off the field, the two batters share a growing obsession with coffee, one that began during India's 2024-25 tour of Australia and has now turned the dressing room into a brewing station of sorts. What started as a search for the perfect pour in Melbourne soon turned into an obsession with different roasts, beans, filters and brewing equipment.
"I think I deserve the credit for getting all of them, 
KL Rahul
, Dhruv Jurel, into coffee. I think KL probably two or three years ago didn't even drink that much coffee. When we went to Australia, that's where we all really got into coffee. And it became an obsession for all of us.
"And once we came back, we just knew that we wanted that quality of coffee at home. So then it began. Then once you go down the rabbit hole of coffee, there are so many things to explore, so many different types of brewing methods and stuff like that. I'm really keen on coffee. And hopefully someday I would like to have a cafe in Bengaluru," Padikkal told TOI.
India's Devdutt Padikkal and teammate KL Rahul, right, react during play on day three of the first cricket test against India in Wellington, New Zealand, Saturday.
The word spread, and players now carry their own equipment on home and away tours, no longer relying on instant sachets or powders at team hotels. Even during the ongoing series against New Zealand, 
Rahul
, Padikkal, Jurel and Yashasvi Jaiswal, the latest to jump on the coffee bandwagon, are carrying their personal filters because there is no compromise. 
Before connecting bat to ball, that first cup of coffee is non-negotiable.
If Padikkal has influenced Rahul's off-field choices, it is the other way around when the two batters are at the crease. Representing the same state in domestic cricket, they have played plenty of cricket together, and their understanding was evident as they blunted New Zealand on Day 2. Their 165-run stand frustrated the hosts, while their reading of the game was astute.
The left-right pair were happy to negotiate maidens and didn't shy away from finding the release shot, even if it meant Rahul reverse-sweeping Glenn Phillips. They never lost control of the proceedings. New Zealand tried every trick in the book to disrupt their rhythm and concentration, but none worked. It didn't matter whether the wicketkeeper was standing up or back, whether the ball was old or new, or whether the field was attacking or defensive. The two were a picture of concentration.
Only something supernatural could have dislodged them from their assured footing, and Kyle Jamieson found the magic in the 83rd over. It was déjà vu of sorts, as Akash Deep had done something similar to Glenn Phillips earlier in the Test. Padikkal could do little to counter that delivery. The left-hander lost his stumps just as he was within striking distance of a hundred and made sure to check the replay on the giant screen before walking off.
After a job well done for the team, the coffee machine in the dressing room will be put to work. Dhruv Jurel is unlikely to be on barista duty, with the wicketkeeper-batter presumably padded up, but Jaiswal now has enough time on his hands to perfect the pour for his teammate. A fitting reward for a job well done.

briefs.headline: Provide RTI documents free of cost if fee notice delayed, says Keralam Information Commissioner
briefs.bodyText:
Provide RTI documents free of cost if fee notice delayed, says Keralam Information Commissioner
Ramakrishnan also clarified that applicants are required to pay a fee only while filing an RTI application and that no fee is needed for submitting appeals.
Kozhikode: Keralam Information Commissioner T K Ramakrishnan has directed public authorities to provide documents sought under the Right to Information (RTI) Act free of cost if they fail to notify applicants about copying charges within the prescribed time.
Addressing reporters after a district-level hearing at the Kozhikode Collectorate on Friday, he said authorities were required to notify applicants within the stipulated period if any fee was payable for providing copies of requested records.
"If they failed to do so, the entire set of documents sought by the applicant should be supplied free of charge," he said.
The hearing saw the disposal of 20 appeal petitions, according to a statement issued by the Commission.
Ramakrishnan also clarified that applicants are required to pay a fee only while filing an RTI application and that no fee is needed for submitting appeals.
He stressed the need for public authorities to ensure that replies to RTI applications were complete and contained all mandatory particulars.
These include the dates of receipt of the application and issue of the reply, the name and designation of the Public Information Officer, the officer's signature, PAN, office seal, telephone number and email address.
In cases where copying charges were applicable, the reply should specify the cost per page, total number of pages, total amount payable and the relevant head of account for making the payment.
The address of the appellate authority and the time limit for filing an appeal should also be clearly mentioned, he said.
The Commissioner asked officials to comply with Section 4 of the RTI Act by proactively disclosing information and keeping departmental websites updated.
He also cautioned that misuse of the RTI Act would not be allowed.

briefs.headline: Odanadi appeals to Pope for independent probe into child abuse case
briefs.bodyText:
Odanadi appeals to Pope for independent probe into child abuse case
In a letter addressed to Pope Leo XIV through the Apostolic Nuncio to India, K V Stanly, Founder Secretary of Odanadi, urged the Vatican to intervene in the matter and ensure justice for the alleged victims.
Mangaluru: Odanadi Seva Samsthe, an organisation working for the rescue and rehabilitation of women and children affected by human trafficking and sexual exploitation, appealed to Pope Leo XIV to order an independent investigation into allegations of child sexual abuse involving a priest in the Diocese of Mangaluru.
In a letter addressed to Pope Leo XIV through the Apostolic Nuncio to India, K V Stanly, Founder Secretary of Odanadi, urged the Vatican to intervene in the matter and ensure justice for the alleged victims.
According to the letter, several families from the Diocese of Mangaluru had approached Odanadi with serious complaints alleging that a local priest had sexually abused minor boys. The families also reportedly alleged that when they approached diocesan authorities seeking intervention, they faced inaction and pressure to remain silent.
Stanly clarified that the appeal did not presume anyone's guilt and stressed that the allegations must be investigated through a fair, impartial and lawful process. However, he expressed concern over the alleged lack of response and the fear and helplessness experienced by the affected families.
The letter urged Pope Leo XIV to take three key steps. First, it called for an independent investigation by an authority outside the local diocesan administration, citing concerns over the handling of the complaints.
Second, it sought immediate protection, professional psychological counselling and pastoral support for the alleged victims and their families. It stressed that they should be allowed to speak freely without intimidation or pressure to withdraw their complaints, while maintaining strict confidentiality regarding the children's identities.
Third, Odanadi urged the Church to adopt precautionary safeguarding measures by temporarily removing individuals facing credible allegations of child sexual abuse from active duties involving children, pending the completion of civil and Church investigations. The letter clarified that such a measure should not be treated as a declaration of guilt but as a preventive step to protect children.
Stanly stated that Odanadi was prepared to cooperate with any investigation initiated by the Holy See and was also engaging with Indian civil authorities under relevant child-protection laws, including the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and the Juvenile Justice Act.
The organisation expressed its willingness to share relevant information through secure and confidential channels to safeguard the identities of the children concerned.

briefs.headline: ‘We will not allow that’: Trump warns Iran over ‘rumour’ of Tehran's dirty bomb plot
briefs.bodyText:
US president 
Donald Trump
 on Friday said the United States would find out if Iran was attempting to build a dirty bomb and would prevent it, referring to reports of a potential Iranian plot involving the weapon.
“There is a rumour that they're building a dirty bomb,” Trump remarked during a White House press conference. “We know a lot about what's happening in Iran. We know everything they say. We know who they are, where they are. We'll find out about it. We will not allow that,” he added.
CNN had earlier reported that US intelligence indicated Iran could be attempting to build a dirty bomb and detonate it in Washington. Reuters said it had not independently verified the report. Iran's Foreign Ministry denied the allegations on Tuesday, describing them as “baseless”.
A dirty bomb combines conventional explosives with radioactive material to spread contamination. It is less destructive than a nuclear weapon, which relies on a fission reaction.
Trump's remarks were more measured than his warning earlier this week, when he said Iran would “pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before” if it targeted members of his administration with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in the US capital.
The US president also reiterated Washington's opposition to Iran acquiring nuclear weapons.
“Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, ever,” he said.
Trump also claimed that the United States had “total control” over the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil shipments, and said the US Navy had imposed a blockade.
“Last week, we took out record amounts of oil from the Hormuz Strait. Our navy has a blockade,” he said. “We have total control over the Hormuz Strait.”
His remarks came as Iranian authorities continued to insist that vessels must follow their prescribed protocol to transit the waterway or risk being attacked.
Trump also linked US petrol prices to the outcome of negotiations with Tehran, claiming that Iran wanted an agreement but was unwilling to accept Washington's terms.
“The prices of gasoline now also depend on how we settle up with Iran. They want to make a deal, but they don't want to make a deal that's acceptable to me,” he said, adding that the US wanted “a real deal, not a fake deal”.

briefs.headline: India looks beyond borders to secure critical minerals, says mines secretary
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India is exploring opportunities to secure critical mineral supplies through both domestic resources and overseas investments, ministry of mines secretary Keshav Chandra said, underlining the government's efforts to strengthen mineral security through policy reforms, exploration and international partnerships.
Speaking at a closed-door industry interaction organised by the mines ministry and the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), Chandra outlined the government's reform agenda to improve the global competitiveness of the mining sector. According to news agency ANI, the focus areas include geological exploration, responsible mining, advanced processing, research, recycling and technology-enabled governance.
Chandra also highlighted recent auction reforms, including the relaxation of minimum bidder requirements for certain minerals and the automatic issuance of Letters of Intent. Responding to industry concerns, he discussed measures already undertaken and those under consideration to address operational challenges in developing mineral blocks.
He urged companies to explore the extraction of critical minerals from alternative resources, including red mud, an industrial residue generated during aluminium production.
The interaction also saw the launch of a concept paper titled Enabling Overseas Investment in Critical Minerals: Policy, Financial and Institutional Framework for Securing India's Critical Mineral Supply Chains.
Chandra said the paper's focus on moving from memorandums of understanding (MoUs) to actual project delivery was aligned with the ministry's efforts, including the overseas engagements of Khanij Bidesh India Ltd (KABIL). He expressed interest in examining the recommendations made in the paper.
On overseas investments, the secretary emphasised the need for enabling mechanisms to improve project viability. He said the ministry would continue addressing industry concerns through policy and regulatory reforms, institutional coordination and targeted interventions.

Opening the interaction, Pankaj Satija, Co-Chair of the FICCI Mining Committee and Executive Vice-President of JSW, welcomed the ministry's reforms in exploration, mineral auctions and mine operationalisation.
Satija also flagged growing vulnerabilities in global supply chains arising from export controls, domestic value-addition requirements and restrictions on processing technologies. He stressed the need for diversified and resilient mineral supply chains to support India's industrial and economic security.
According to FICCI, the concept paper was prepared following a mandate from the Ministry of Mines and draws on research and stakeholder consultations. It identifies barriers to overseas mineral investments and proposes solutions, including a Country-Priority Mineral Matrix and a tiered framework to prioritise projects for government support.
The paper also calls for stronger institutional coordination, streamlined approvals and closer integration of overseas investments with India's domestic processing and manufacturing capabilities.

briefs.headline: 'To protect integrity': CA drops big statement on Cummins captaincy
briefs.deck: The CA Board resolved to express its unanimous support for Pat Cummins as captain
briefs.bodyText:
Cricket Australia (CA) has thrown its support behind 
Pat Cummins
, confirming that he will remain Australia's Test captain for the New Zealand series next month despite allegations from former teammates about his involvement in the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal.
The CA board met on Friday (local time) to discuss Cummins' position as captain and decided to back the 33-year-old unanimously. CA chair 
David Boon
 and CEO Todd Greenberg also met Cummins in Sydney to discuss his welfare, the support needed by the team and the upcoming series against New Zealand.
“The CA Board met to ensure measures are in place to protect the integrity of Australian cricket and the welfare of all concerned. As part of this meeting, the Board resolved to express its unanimous support for Pat Cummins as captain given ongoing speculation about his position,” a CA statement read.
“CA chair David Boon and CEO Todd Greenberg met with Cummins in Sydney on Friday and discussed several issues including his welfare, support required for the team and the forthcoming series against New Zealand.”
Boon said the board wanted to guide Australian cricket through the controversy while allowing players and support staff to share any information they had about the 2018 tour of South Africa.
Boon said the forum announced earlier this week would provide an opportunity for those involved in the tour to discuss their accounts. 
CA has said it will publish the forum's Terms of Reference in due course.
“That’s what the independent forum we announced this week is about and the board encourages all players and support staff to tell and discuss their stories there. We will be publishing the Terms of Reference in due course,” Boon said.
“We’ve expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa.
“We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat’s integrity has been compromised.”
Cummins also issued a statement thanking Boon and Greenberg for their support. He said being Australia's captain was a responsibility he had always taken seriously and welcomed the board's decision to speak to him and other players and staff involved in the 2018 tour.
“It meant a lot to speak with David and Todd today. Being Australian captain carries with it an awesome responsibility. I never have and never will take that lightly,” Cummins said.
“David and Todd have a very tough job navigating cricket through all of this and I commend them for reaching out to me and to many of the players and staff from 2018.”
Cummins also said he fully supported the independent forum and would attend to hear what players and staff had to say about the events of the South Africa tour.
“There will be a lot of difficult conversations but that is what’s needed,” Cummins said.
“Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority."
Cummins, along with the rest of the touring squad in 2018, has faced allegations that he knew sandpaper was being used illegally on the ball to generate reverse swing.
Cameron Bancroft and Usman Khawaja have said “we all knew” about the ball-tampering, with David Warner and Chadd Sayers also backing their claims.
Cummins rejected Khawaja's allegations in his memoir, Sabr, describing the claim that the entire team knew about the 2018 Sandpapergate plan as "100 per cent wrong" and "complete and utter nonsense".

briefs.headline: 'Look at India': President Donald Trump calls for lower interest rates in US to boost economic growth
briefs.bodyText:
Pointing to high economic growth in India, President Donald Trump said on Friday that the US could achieve economic growth in the range of 14-15 per cent if it had lower interest rates.
"Look at India, they have low interest rates, and they have a seven per cent growth rate," Trump said, adding that the US could achieve economic growth in the range of 14-15 per cent if it had lower interest rates.
He made the comments during his visit to Manila, where he secured two trade deals with Thailand and the Philippines, and added that around 10 more agreements were expected soon.
"In four days, I met more than 20 world leaders, secured two new trade deals, and about 10 others coming very soon," Trump told a press conference at the White House here.
Trump also referred to his meeting with the leaders of the Quad group comprising the US, India, Japan and Australia.
"We announced the first-ever Quad Bureau Leaders' Forum to cooperate on matters of economic security, we launched a Quad SI Accelerator, and we agreed to a new collaboration on maritime security and surveillance operations" Trump said.
India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of the trade agreement in February. However, changes in the tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.
India is seeking lower tariffs for its goods in the US market than its competitor nations such as Bangladesh, Vietnam and Cambodia.

briefs.headline: Why did Tukaram Mundhe withdraw his petition after dragging the Centre to court? | Explained
briefs.deck: How does the jurisdiction issue between FSSAI and FDA affect businesses and consumers? The history behind the tussle and how Maharashtra had raised concerns earlier too
briefs.bodyText:
A constitutional battle waged by Maharashtra’s Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe has been withdrawn. In September this year, the FDA had filed a case in the Bombay High Court, accusing the Centre of usurping its power by creating a parallel system. It hindered the work of the State government in protecting the consumers’ interests, the FDA said. Adding that it impeded the work of the FDA officials by stopping them from independently raiding establishments which have been licensed by the Centre. Tukaram Mundhe’s step had created a stir, pitting the Centre and the State of Maharashtra against each other over jurisdiction issues.
It also accused the FSSAI of ‘clandestinely’ adding new regulations. But now, the FDA Commissioner has decided to withdraw the petition. What do the documents accessed by The Hindu reveal? And why did Tukaram Mundhe decide to withdraw the plea? How do experts weigh in on the constitutional debate? And what does it mean for the businesses and for consumers? Is this the first time Maharashtra has raised this issue?
At the heart of the petition filed by the Maharashtra FDA in the Bombay High Court on September 3, 2026, is a jurisdictional dispute. The FDA has argued in the petition that the Centre has gone against the grain of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, to create a parallel structure of enforcement, usurping the powers of the State FDA. It has claimed that the Act itself had envisaged decentralisation of power and had delegated the executive powers of implementation to the State authorities.
According to the petition, the core of the dispute is the constitutional validity of regulations and the positions created by FSSAI (Food Safety and Standards Authority of India). Maharashtra government argued that this encroached upon the responsibilities of the State authority in food safety enforcement. The State government said that FSSAI’s move was geared towards centralisation of enforcement, and contradicted the decentralised framework envisioned by the FSS Act. It pointed to the original Statement of Objects and Reasons of the Food Safety Act, which talked of the decentralisation of licensing for food products, empowering the States to issue registration and State licences.
Maharashtra government said that the new regulations and new positions hindered the effective protection of public health and consumer interests within the State. The petition challenged the constitutional validity of a few provisions of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011 and its amendment in 2026. It also challenged the creation of the posts of Food Analysts and Central Food Safety Officers under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (Recruitment and Appointment) Regulation, 2018.

briefs.headline: Oregon mother sues couple for $8.7m after son loses eye on e-bike at sleepover
briefs.deck: A negligence lawsuit has emerged following a tragic e-bike accident involving a 14-year-old boy during a birthday sleepover hosted by Tessa and Matthew Cohen. The allegations claim that the Cohens provided electric bikes without adequate supervision or safety protocols. As a result, the boy sustained life-altering injuries, requiring significant medical attention. The lawsuit demands $8.7 million…
briefs.bodyText:
A birthday sleepover in Oregon has become the centre of an $8.7 million negligence lawsuit after a 14-year-old boy suffered life-changing injuries in an electric bicycle crash. His mother, Alexis Nicoli, has filed a case against the parents who allegedly provided the children with e-bikes during the gathering. The incident, which took place in November 2025, was reported by KOIN 6 News and The Oregonian, with further details published by the Lake Oswego Review. According to the lawsuit, Nicoli’s son was attending a birthday sleepover at the home of Tessa and Matthew Cohen in the Portland area, along with another friend. The gathering was being held for the Cohens’ son, and the couple allegedly made several electric bicycles available to the boys to ride.
The accident occurred while the children were riding together. Nicoli’s son reportedly lost control of the e-bike and crashed, sustaining severe injuries to his head and right eye. He was wearing a helmet at the time, according to the complaint. The teenager was rushed to hospital, where doctors identified multiple injuries, including a fracture to the inner wall of his right eye socket. 
The impact also caused a rupture that resulted in cerebrospinal fluid leaking from the area surrounding his brain and spinal cord.
His injuries were so extensive that his right eye could not be saved. Doctors eventually replaced it with an orbital silicone sphere. The lawsuit also describes the extensive medical treatment required to address the damage to his skull and the surrounding structures. Nicoli is seeking $8.7 million in damages, arguing that the injuries have caused significant physical and psychological trauma and will affect her son’s life for years to come.
Why the parents are being sued
The lawsuit accuses the Cohens of negligence, alleging that they allowed children who were not legally old enough to ride the electric bicycles to use them without adequate supervision. It also claims that the couple failed to establish whether the bikes were suitable and safe for the boys, provide proper instructions for their use or take reasonable precautions to prevent an accident. The case places particular emphasis on the responsibility of adults hosting children at their homes, especially when potentially dangerous recreational equipment is made available to young guests. The Cohens had not publicly responded to the allegations when KOIN 6 News published its report. The claims in the lawsuit have not been established in court.
What Oregon’s e-bike rules say
Oregon has specific age restrictions for electric bicycle riders, with the rules depending on the classification of the vehicle. Under the regulations applicable at the time of the November 2025 accident, riders generally had to be at least 16 to operate Class 2 and Class 3 e-bikes. 
Class 1 bicycles, which provide motor assistance only while pedalling and stop assisting at 20 mph, had a separate exemption for younger riders under the state’s earlier legislation.
Further changes under House Bill 4007 will allow riders aged 14 and 15 to operate Class 1 e-bikes from January 1, 2027, while the minimum age for Class 2 and Class 3 models remains 16. The distinction could be significant in the lawsuit, as the precise classification of the bicycles provided to the children will be relevant to the allegations surrounding their use.
As the case moves forward, the lawsuit is likely to draw attention to the responsibilities of parents who provide electric bicycles to children, particularly when hosting gatherings where several young riders may be involved.

stories.headline: Dommasandra Circle, SH-168 need urgent fix, say Bengaluru techies in Sarjapur
stories.deck: Residents of Sarjapur are advocating for immediate safety improvements on state highway 168 due to frequent accidents. They have expressed concerns regarding potholes, poor visibility, and inadequate traffic management at the junction of Sarjapur Road and SH-35. The Save Sarjapura group reported that road widening efforts have stagnated for 15 years, contributing to dangerous conditions.…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Residents of Sarjapur are pressing for urgent safety measures on state highway 168, the Chandapura-Dommasandra road linking Whitefield and Electronics City, calling the stretch dangerous. Frequent accidents, potholes and vehicles crashing into medians every month or two have made the road unsafe for techies who use it to reach Whitefield and Electronics City.
In an email sent last month to Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda, the Save Sarjapura group flagged the junction of Sarjapur Road and SH-35 (Dommasandra-Varthur Road) as one of the most important in southeast Bengaluru. It connects Sarjapur corridor and its school district with Whitefield on one side and Electronics City and Hosur Road on the other. The group urged govt to expedite the work.
Accidents on SH-168
Half of the 10km stretch on SH-168 is a narrow, winding single lane each way with no divider. Its S-curves and inadequate width make it prone to accidents, with road widening stuck for about 15 years. The other half has four lanes and a divider, but potholes and invisible concrete medians send vehicles crashing into dividers every month or two. At Muthanallur signal on SH-35, half-foot-deep potholes, waterlogging and poorly built storm water drains add to the misery.
 Mukund from Save Sarjapura said: "We want safe roads. We have met the city traffic police joint commissioner several times over the years. Traffic police extended its jurisdiction to Dommasandra Circle last year, but said the 10km stretch in between is not covered."
The junction is so wide that traffic personnel are not visible from some directions, confusing motorists, particularly at night. "At times, we have just one traffic policeman managing this busy intersection," said Joy VR of Sarjapur RWA.
Dommasandra flyover has remained incomplete since 2020, and the junction has no storm-water outlets after a nearby waterbody was flattened to stock material for the project. Joy VR also called for curbs on concrete mixers, construction vehicles and inter-state heavy transport during peak hours, along with more traffic police.

stories.headline: Karnataka high court quashes case against MedPlus directors over Rs 1 tablet shortage
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Karnataka high court has quashed proceedings against MedPlus director P Srinivas and in-charge director M Surendranath over a 10-year-old criminal case of a short supply of a tablet valued at about Rs 1.
Journalist Shrinath Josh claimed in his complaint that on Aug 23, 2016, though in the bill raised by the petitioners, an amount of Rs 40.3 was collected for eight 15 mg Lanzol Junior tablets, the accused had supplied only seven tablets and an excess amount of Rs 1.1 was collected by them.
“The proceedings were pending before the 3rd additional metropolitan magistrate of the city.
Justice S Vishwajit Shetty has noted in his recent order, “In the case on hand, the allegation against the accused petitioners is that they had supplied seven tablets instead of eight tablets and they had collected an excess amount of Rs 1.1 from the complainant. It is not the case of the prosecution that the accused persons had collected an amount in excess of the price indicated on the label of the container or pack thereof, whichever is less.”
“Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that prosecution of the petitioners would not only cause embarrassment to them, but would also amount to abuse of process of law,” the judge observed while allowing the petition.

stories.headline: CM’s agenda for Bengaluru police: Zero tolerance for drugs, hate speech and traffic congestion
stories.bodyText:
After the restructuring of Bengaluru City Police, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday held the first meeting with the officers deputed to the city police and directed zero tolerance towards drugs, hate speech and traffic congestion. He further strictly warned against “real estate” dealings at police stations.
“When the Police Commissioner’s office was started in Bengaluru, the population was around 20 lakh. Now, the population has reached approximately 1.5 crore. We have established five police commissionerates to manage this effectively. Under the Chief Commissioner, five Police Commissioners will manage the city’s law and order. We have also expanded its jurisdiction by adding a few police stations,” he said.
“Similarly, we have worked to strengthen the police force by creating hundreds of new posts. You must work as ‘Team Bengaluru’ to live up to the government’s expectations,” he said. “There should be no internal conflicts or corruption in the department,” he added.
Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said the creation of five police commissionerates in Bengaluru was a historic decision aimed at making the city’s policing system more effective and directing senior officers to prioritise law and order and crack down on drug trafficking, rowdyism and crimes against women. He said that the creation of five police commissionerates will make policing in Bengaluru more effective both administratively and operationally.
Dr. Parameshwara said Bengaluru’s global reputation and its position as an investment destination depended on political stability, peace and effective law and order. He referred to a recent report in an international newspaper on the city’s traffic problems and said that the developments in Bengaluru attracted global attention and everyone had a responsibility to protect its image.
Meanwhile, Home Minister Priyank Kharge held a separate discussion with senior police officers and the newly appointed commissioners of the five police commissionerates on strengthening the city’s policing system. The meeting discussed preparing an action plan for the new commissionerates and improving coordination among police units. He also discussed strengthening administrative efficiency and making policing more citizen-centric.

stories.headline: Bengaluru Police Commissionerate restructuring leaves some divisions overburdened and others underutilised
stories.deck: The newly created Peenya division has been the biggest casualty. Under the supervision of a single DCP, the division, which falls under the West Commissionerate, has only four police stations
stories.bodyText:
The restructuring of the Bengaluru City Police Commissionerate into five parts has not only created confusion over the reporting structure, but has also resulted in an uneven distribution of police stations across divisions, with no clear rationale behind how stations were grouped.
The newly created Peenya division has been the biggest casualty. Under the supervision of a single Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), the division, which falls under the West Commissionerate, has only four police stations: Peenya, Byadarahalli, Rajagopalnagar and Madanayakanahalli. Whitefield and East divisions had faced a similar situation, with five and six police stations, respectively.
Four police stations are usually handled by a single Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP). Ironically, the ACP of the Vijayanagar subdivision, which also falls under the West Commissionerate, oversees five police stations, one more than the DCP of Peenya.
Further, there had been a proposal to bring the Nelamangala police station within city limits. Its jurisdiction lies immediately beyond that of the Madanayakanahalli police station, and it could have been brought under city limits and placed within the Peenya division, but this was not done.
Moreover, the West Commissionerate has two other divisions, West and Kengeri, which have 13 and 11 police stations, respectively. A senior police officer said the Peenya division could have shared the burden of the other two divisions, which would have ensured that all three divisions had eight to nine police stations each. He described the exercise as “conceived without any ground-level understanding and background work”.
“The uneven division is a result of a hurried restructuring exercise. The exercise is not data-backed, and there have not been enough discussions,” he said.
Many stations ignored
Earlier this year, there was a proposal to add at least 15 more law-and-order police stations from the adjoining Bengaluru Rural and Bengaluru South district police units to the Bengaluru City Commissionerate.
The rationale was that these areas had largely urbanised, yet continued to be governed by rural police units. Seven of those police stations have now been added.
The police stations left out are Nelamangala, Doddaballapur, Devanahalli, Vijayapura, Vishwanathapura, Hoskote, Bidadi, Tavarekere and Kaggalipura. A senior police officer familiar with the developments said the stations left out were still considered semi-urban.
However, most of these areas have witnessed rapid commercialisation and the development of new layouts. In addition, several of them fall within the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) area.
Further, KWIN City is coming up in the Doddaballapur belt, which is likely to see further residential development. In Bidadi, a mega AI city project, known as the Greater Bidadi Integrated Township, is also coming up. However, the police stations covering these areas have not been included.
No reports, through proposals
Before the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) was restructured into five corporations, the government had constituted the Brand Bengaluru Committee, which carried out the exercise, backed by data and stakeholder consultations, and submitted a report.
The government subsequently reviewed the report, considered multiple options, and finally settled on five civic bodies under a single coordinating authority.
According to Police Department insiders, several officers are unhappy with the restructuring and feel that the process was hurriedly completed without wider consultations.

briefs.headline: Karnataka high court refuses to toss case over witness count
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Karnataka high court has ruled that the presence of only four witnesses to an alleged incident is not, by itself, grounds to reject the prosecution case at the chargesheet stage.
Justice Suraj Govindaraj dismissed a petition filed by a Bengaluru resident, his father, sister, co-sister and neighbour challenging criminal proceedings initiated on his wife’s complaint alleging cruelty, criminal intimidation and other offences.
The couple got married in 2022. The wife alleged that she discovered her husband was having an extramarital affair with his sister-in-law. Although she persuaded him to move from Chikkaballapur to Bengaluru, the situation did not change, she alleged.
The petitioners argued that the case relied on only four witnesses — the complainant, her parents and one independent witness — and that her initial allegations were doubtful.
The court noted that police had filed the chargesheet after completing their investigation. The complaint contained specific allegations concerning an incident on March 1, 2024, including that the petitioners assaulted the complainant, tore her clothes, poured petrol on her and attempted to set her on fire. 
She also alleged that they snatched her gold chain.
The judge said these were not general or omnibus accusations but referred to specific acts allegedly committed by the petitioners. The complaint and witness statements couldn’t be considered wholly insufficient to proceed against them, the court observed.
The petitioners’ contentions involved disputed questions of fact that must be considered during trial, the court said.

briefs.headline: Bike taxis to return as SC bins Karnataka plea against HC order
briefs.deck: The Supreme Court has dismissed the Karnataka government's appeal against the ban on bike taxis. As a result, bike taxis will operate in Bengaluru under regulatory conditions. Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh indicated that rules for these services will be established. The government is prioritizing passenger safety, especially for women commuters, in this regulatory framework. Proposed…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Bike taxis will ply on the roads of Bengaluru and other parts of Karnataka, subject to applicable permits and regulatory requirements, after 
Supreme Court
 on Friday dismissed the state govt's appeal against a Karnataka HC judgment that set aside the blanket ban on such services.
A bench comprising Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh, after an elaborate hearing of arguments of different parties, including the cab aggregators, dismissed the special leave petition filed by govt against the Jan 23 order of the high court.
Transport minister Byrathi Suresh said that in the wake of the SC order, he has instructed officials to frame rules with applicable conditions. "The department has been instructed to frame the necessary rules to regulate bike-taxi operations. Passenger safety, particularly that of women commuters, would be the govt's priority," he said.
Govt is considering imposing several conditions on bike-taxi operations, he said. The proposed regulations are likely to include verification of bike-taxi riders' documents, installation of GPS devices, mandatory vehicle insurance and checks on other required documents.
Transport minister Byrathi Suresh said that govt would have to comply with the SC directions. 
“We are waiting for the written order to discuss the matter with the advocate general.”
While pronouncing the decision of the bench, SC judge Justice Sharma even recalled a conversation he had with women staff in his office, who use bike taxis to commute. “I asked them, ‘How do you come to my office?’ They said on a motorbike because they do not have the money to hire a cab. I asked them, ‘Why don’t you take an auto?’ They said, ‘Sir, it is five times (the fare)’,” Justice Sharma told the lawyers appearing in the matter. “A bike taxi is safer for young girls as it has GPS. It is better to regulate it than ban it. Bike taxis are already there in 25 states of the country,” Justice Sharma added.
Karnataka high court had directed the state govt to consider the applications seeking licence to operate bike taxi services, while reserving liberty to impose necessary conditions. A division bench comprising Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice CM Joshi had also set aside the order passed by a single bench on April 1, 2025, which said bike taxis could not legally operate in Karnataka unless and until the state framed the required regulatory framework.
Challenging the division bench order before the Supreme Court, the state govt had argued that HC’s order proceeded on an erroneous interpretation of the statutory scheme under the MV Act, particularly Sections 66, 74, and 80, by effectively reducing the discretionary powers of the state and regional transport authorities to grant or refuse permits to a mere formality.

briefs.headline: Partial relief for head constable as Karnataka high court says criminal process must follow law
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Karnataka high court has quashed a magistrate’s order summoning a Bengaluru head constable and remanded the case for fresh proceedings, holding that mandatory safeguards for public servants under Section 223(2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) had not been followed.
Justice M Nagaprasanna partly allowed a petition by head constable Shivashankar, observing that criminal proceedings must follow the path prescribed by the legislature and courts cannot dispense with statutory safeguards merely because proceedings are preliminary.
Shivashankar was posted at Bandepalya police station last year when complainant MD Anil Kumar organised a Karaga Mahotsav at Mangammanapalya. Kumar alleged that Shivashankar and two other police personnel used filthy and abusive language against participants, disturbing public tranquillity and causing nuisance.
Kumar filed a private complaint, following which the magistrate recorded his sworn statement on Sept 25, 2025. On Dec 12, the magistrate issued summons to Shivashankar and the two other accused.
Shivashankar contended that BNSS Section 223(2) required the magistrate, before taking cognisance of allegations against a public servant concerning official duties, to hear the public servant and obtain a report on the incident from a superior officer. 
He also argued that prior prosecution sanction mandated under Section 218 had not been obtained.
Justice Nagaprasanna held that the defect was not the absence of sanction under Section 218, but the failure to follow the mandatory procedure under Section 223(2). The court said the special procedure prescribed for complaints against public servants over acts connected with official functions couldn’t be ignored, as doing so would render the safeguard meaningless.
Quashing the magistrate’s Dec 12, 2025 order, the high court directed the magistrate to restart the procedure from the stage after recording Kumar’s sworn statement on Sept 25, 2025.

briefs.headline: Karnataka slashed funds for welfare of persons with disabilities, say rights groups
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Allocations for several welfare schemes for persons with disabilities (PwDs) in 
Karnataka
 have been drastically reduced over the years, advocacy groups alleged at a conference on the implementation of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, inaugurated Friday.
Funding for the free laptop scheme fell by half from Rs 4 crore in 2014 to Rs 2 crore in 2026-27, while allocations for hostels for working women with visual impairments were cut by nearly 66%, said N Annavaram, assistant professor at University of Hyderabad, who is visually impaired.
“Even as some southern states take a cue from Karnataka for its measures to empower PwDs, the drastic reduction of funds is concerning,” he said.
Annavaram urged the state govt to consider progressive amendments to the Act to increase reservations and make accessibility mandatory. The Act provides for 4% reservation in govt employment for PwDs. “Many positions identified for the totally blind are being arbitrarily given to candidates with low vision,” he said.
Legislative council chairman Saleem Ahmed assured the advocacy groups that he would facilitate a discussion on measures to empower PwDs and address gaps in the implementation of govt schemes during the upcoming legislature session in Belagavi.
Chief secretary Shalini Rajneesh, who inaugurated the conference, said the state govt had presented its implementation of the Act to the UN Special Rapporteur on the Rights of PwDs, who had lauded Karnataka’s initiatives.
She stressed the importance of preventing disabilities wherever possible through timely intervention. Recalling how visually impaired students had sought voice-to-text equipment to reduce their dependence on scribes, she appreciated their efforts to become independent.
“Our approach should not be one of charity, but of empowerment and facilitation,” she said.
“The decision to purchase 5,000 laptops was taken by the cabinet Thursday under the minorities department. Others will also follow suit,” she told TOI, responding to the concerns raised by the advocacy groups.
The conference was held ahead of the RPwD Act completing a decade since its passage by Parliament. Gautam Agarwal, general secretary of National Federation of the Blind (NFB), Karnataka, Mitra Jyoti managing trustee Madhu Singhal and representatives of Karnataka Rajya Andha Noukarara Sangha also participated in the event.

briefs.headline: Man who gave kidney to save wife loses her in Bengaluru hit-and-run
briefs.deck: Veenabai, aged 38, tragically perished in a hit-and-run accident close to Nelamangala. She was driving home with her husband, Shivaji Rao, after visiting Siddaganga Mutt. Shivaji had heroically donated a kidney two years earlier to save her life. The untimely loss leaves him shattered. The police are currently looking into the incident by reviewing CCTV footage to locate the vehicle involved in…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: In a heartwrenching tragedy that has left a family shattered, a 38-year-old woman whose life was saved two years ago after her husband donated one of his kidneys to her was killed in a hitand-run accident near Nelamangala late Thursday night.
The deceased has been identified as Veenabai, a resident of Laggere in Bengaluru.
The fatal mishap occurred near Yedehalli in Nelamangala taluk while she and her husband, Shivaji Rao, were returning home after offering prayers at Siddaganga Mutt in Tumakuru.
According to preliminary police reports, an unidentified goods vehicle rammed into them and sped away, killing Veenabai on the spot. For Shivaji Rao, who works at a private firm, the loss is an unimaginable blow after years of fighting to keep his wife alive.
Four to six years ago, Veenabai suffered severe health complications triggered by low blood pressure, resulting in the failure of both her kidneys. Refusing to give up on the love of his life, Shivaji stepped forward two years ago to donate one of his own kidneys, giving her a second lease on life.
The couple had visited Siddaganga Mutt to express their gratitude and seek blessings for her continued recovery, unaware that tragedy awaited them on their journey back.
Inconsolable at the scene, Shivaji broke down beside his wife’s body.
“I gave her a part of myself just to see her smile and live a full life again; destiny snatched her away from me forever,” a grieving Shivaji said, leaving onlookers and relatives in tears.
Nelamangala traffic police rushed to the spot upon receiving information and shifted the body to Nelamangala govt hospital mortuary for a post-mortem examination.
A case of hit-and-run has been registered and police are scanning CCTV footage along the highway stretch.

briefs.headline: Bike taxis offer relief from steep auto fares, say commuters after SC ruling
briefs.deck: The apex court on Friday dismissed the Karnataka government’s appeal against a High Court order recognising bike taxis as a form of public transport, clearing a major legal hurdle for aggregators such as Ola, Uber and Rapido to resume their services.
briefs.bodyText:
For commuters tired of paying steep auto fares and drivers who lost their livelihoods after bike taxis were banned in Karnataka, the Supreme Court’s decision to allow bike taxis in the State has come as a major relief.
The apex court on Friday dismissed the Karnataka government’s appeal against a High Court order recognising bike taxis as a form of public transport, clearing a major legal hurdle for aggregators such as Ola, Uber and Rapido to resume their services.
A Bench headed by Justice Satish Chandra Sharma dismissed the State government’s appeal against the High Court’s decision. Observing that “regulation was preferable to a blanket ban”, the Bench noted that bike taxis equipped with GPS could offer a safe mode of transport. It also pointed out that two-wheeler taxi services were already operating in 25 States.
Welcome move
Adi Narayana M., president of the Bike Taxi Welfare Association, said the decision marked the end of a prolonged struggle and would bring relief to lakhs of drivers who depend on bike taxis for their livelihood. Welcoming the ruling, Rapido said it affirmed the need for accessible mobility solutions, while Uber said it brought much-needed regulatory clarity and recognised bike taxis as an affordable and convenient option for commuters and a source of flexible earnings for drivers.
Affordable fares
Shrestha M., a commuter, said bike taxis made it easier to reach destinations at a fraction of the cost of taking an autorickshaw. She said auto and cab fares could be exorbitant, with drivers often demanding “extra tips”, particularly at certain locations and during particular hours.
Pooja Kumari, another commuter, said the availability of alternatives such as bike taxis would ensure “much-needed competition” and prevent auto and cab drivers from taking advantage of passengers. She pointed out that none of the autorickshaws run on meters, while even app-based aggregators did not always explain how fares were calculated, with prices varying by time and location even for the same distance.
However, autorickshaw drivers have opposed the decision, arguing that the return of bike taxis would affect their earnings.
T.M. Rudramurthy, general secretary of the Auto Rickshaw Drivers’ Union (ARDU), said allowing bike taxis would go against the interests of autorickshaw and taxi drivers and could push many into financial hardship. He argued that the State government should have made a stronger case before the Supreme Court, highlighting that more than 1.5 lakh autorickshaw drivers depended on the profession for their livelihood.
He also argued that autorickshaws remained a feasible option as they could accommodate more passengers, unlike bike taxis, which can carry only one passenger.
Reacting to the Supreme Court’s order on bike taxis, Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh said, “The government will take a decision on allowing bike taxis after framing several rules and conditions.”
He said the State government would have to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions. However, a final decision would be taken after holding another round of discussions with the Advocate-General.
The Transport Department officials had already been instructed to frame the necessary rules in this regard, he said.
“The safety of bike taxi passengers, particularly women, was the government’s priority. Accordingly, the documents of bike taxi operators, installation of GPS devices, vehicle insurance and other relevant documents would be checked,” he said.

briefs.headline: Karnataka High Court quashes journo-initiated case against pharmacy chain for collecting ₹1.12 in ‘excess’
briefs.deck: The journalist complained that he had placed order for eight tablets but he was supplied with only seven tablets despite collecting the amount for all the eight tablets, and hence it amounted to ‘excess’ pricing
briefs.bodyText:
The High Court of Karnataka has quashed a decade-old criminal proceedings initiated against MedPlus, a unit of Ritemed Pharma Retail Pvt. Ltd., and its directors over allegations that a customer, a senior Kannada television journalist, was overcharged by ₹1.12 after being supplied seven tablets instead of eight while being billed for the eight tablets.
The criminal prosecution under the Clause 26 of the Drugs (Price Control) Order, 2013, was launched by an assistant drug controller acting on the complaint lodged by the journalist on August 26, 2016, after purchasing the tablets from one of the MedPlus medical stores in Bengaluru on August 23, 2016.
The journalist complained that he had placed order for eight tablets but he was supplied with only seven tablets despite collecting the amount for all the eight tablets, and hence it amounted to “excess” pricing.
Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty quashed the case on November 13, 2026, by allowing the petitions filed by the company and its director.
On examining the Clause 26, which prohibits selling any formulation at a price exceeding the price specified in the current price list or on the label of the container or pack, whichever is less, the court said that the Clause 26 would be attracted only when a seller charges more than the specified or labelled price for a drug.
However, the court noted, the prosecution’s allegation itself was that the accused supplied fewer tablets than billed, not that they collected an amount exceeding the price indicated on the label or pack. Consequently, the court said the offence under Clause 26 was not made out based on the complaint lodged by the assistant drugs controller.
The court said that continuing the criminal case would not only amount to an abuse of the process of law but would cause embarrassment to the petitioners.

briefs.headline: Man held for murdering son, attempting to kill wife in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Banashankari police have arrested a 44-year-old man, identified as Sudeep, for allegedly murdering his son and attempting to kill his wife at their apartment in Padmanabhanagar, south Bengaluru.
The incident unfolded between 9 p.m. and 11 p.m. on Monday. The deceased has been identified as Soham Das, 18. His wife, Seema Das, 42, was severely injured. The family had been living in the flat since 2024 and frequently fought, according to the complaint filed by landlord B. Mallaiah.
Neighbours had reportedly complained to the house owner about frequent fights among the family members over the past six months. The owner said he had asked the family several times to resolve their differences peacefully and had also asked them to vacate the house when the fights did not stop.
On Monday, between 9 p.m. and 10 p.m., the owner received calls from neighbours about a disturbance at the apartment. However, when he contacted the security guard after about an hour, he was told that there was no disturbance at the time, so he did not check.
On Thursday, when the owner visited the apartment to speak to the family, there was no response from inside. He subsequently approached the Banashankari police and brought them to the spot. When the police and the owner’s associates opened the locked doors, they found bloodstains on the floor and walls.
Meanwhile, Seema began calling for help from inside a room. When the police opened the door, she allegedly told them that her husband had assaulted her and their son with a knife and a hammer. According to police sources, Seema fell unconscious when he attacked her with a hammer; thinking she was dead, the accused left the place. Soham was found dead in the bathroom.
“Seema is recovering and she is currently out of danger,” an officer said. The Banashankari police have registered an FIR under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, for murder and attempt to murder.

stories.headline: What does EPFO’s Systematic Withdrawal Plan for entail for retirees | Explained
stories.deck: As per the proposed SWP, upon retirement or superannuation, a member will have several options to receive the accumulated PF corpus or a part through periodic withdrawals instead of a lump-sum withdrawal
stories.bodyText:
The Story So Far: The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), in a meeting held in New Delhi on November 19, 2026 approved the Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for EPF members, enabling periodic payouts of retirement savings. As per the proposed SWP, upon retirement or superannuation, a member will have several options to receive the accumulated PF corpus or a part through periodic withdrawals instead of a lump-sum withdrawal.
As of now, a retiring PF subscriber generally withdraws the entire provident fund accumulation as a lump sum. The proposal, cleared by the CBT, say an eligible member, upon retirement, may opt to receive their provident fund accumulations as monthly withdrawals; quarterly withdrawals; half-yearly withdrawals; or annual withdrawals. The remaining corpus will be invested within the EPF Fund and will continue to earn EPF interest on the running balance. The SWP scheme also proposes to provide flexible options to the member for enhancing his or her corpus in PF by voluntary contributions through payroll, direct additional contributions other than payroll and third-party micro-contributions.
