stories.headline: Woman’s Rs 25,000 rebate denied under new regime for capital gains; why ITAT ruled in her favour
stories.deck: A woman filed her income tax return for assessment year 2025-26, declaring a total income of Rs 6,77,511. This included short-term capital gains of Rs 3,97,511 arising from the transfer of listed equity shares. Such gains are taxable u/s 111A of the Act at a special rate of tax. She opted for the new tax regime under Section 115BAC(1A) and claimed a rebate of Rs 25,000 under Section 87A.
stories.bodyText:
Are your short-term capital gains also eligible for a rebate if your overall income falls below Rs 12 lakh? A taxpayer who earned short-term capital gains from listed equity shares has won a dispute over a Rs 25,000 
income tax rebate
 after the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Hyderabad, held in her favour.
The ITAT decision was regarding the availability of rebate under Section 87A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (the ‘Act’), against tax payable on short-term capital gains arising from the transfer of equity shares taxable under Section 111A of Act.
In its November 6, 2026, order, the tribunal ruled that Section 87A of the Income Tax Act, 1961, did not expressly prohibit the rebate in cases where income included short-term capital gains taxable at a special rate under Section 111A. However, there is a catch.
What the case is about
A woman filed her income tax return for assessment year 2025-26, declaring a total income of Rs 6,77,511. This included short-term capital gains of Rs 3,97,511 arising from the transfer of listed equity shares. Such gains are taxable u/s 111A of the Act at a special rate of tax.
She opted for the new tax regime under Section 115BAC(1A) and claimed a rebate of Rs 25,000 under Section 87A. However, when the Centralised Processing Centre (CPC), Bengaluru, processed her return, it determined a tax payable at Rs 75,502 without allowing the rebate.
The assessee challenged the denial before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals). The first appellate authority rejected her explanation and upheld the denial. She then approached the Hyderabad bench of the ITAT.
Her authorised representative argued that neither Section 87A nor Section 115BAC(1A) expressly barred the rebate merely because part of the taxpayer’s income was taxable under Section 111A.
The representative also relied on two earlier tribunal decisions: 
Jayshreeben Jayantibhai Palsana v. ITO
, decided by the ITAT Ahmedabad bench, and 
Pushpa Prakash Misar v. ITO
, decided by the ITAT Mumbai bench. Jayendran’s counsel additionally cited the Bombay High Court decision in 
Chamber of Tax Consultants v. DGIT (Systems)
.
The Revenue opposed the appeal. Its representative relied on CBDT Circular No. 13/2025, dated September 19, 2025, and argued that the rebate was not applicable to taxpayers opting for the new tax regime under Section 115BAC(1A). The department maintained that the lower authorities had correctly rejected the claim.
Why did ITAT rule in favour of assessee?
Tanu Gupta, Partner at Mainstay Tax Advisors LLP says that this judgement is important for the interpretation of Section 87A and the extent to which the rebate can be restricted by Circular No. 13/2025 dated September 19, 2025 issued by the CBDT.
“ITAT was of the opinion that AO and CIT(A) did not have any other reason to disallow the tax rebate u/s 87A of the Act from the tax liability which included tax on short-term capital gains u/s 111A at a special rate,” she says.
Further, on observing the plain language of Section 87A and its provisos, the ITAT was of the opinion that there is no restriction to claim rebate u/s.87A of the Act where the assessee satisfies the other prescribed conditions, such as income being under the applicable threshold even if it includes income taxable at special rate under Section 111A of the Act.
“The Tribunal's decision also relies on past judgments. It was held that there is no express restriction to claim rebate u/s.87A of the Act even in a case of tax payment under the new regime of taxation as per provisions of Sec.115BAC(1A) of the Act,” Gupta tells TOI.
“The ruling is a welcome development for taxpayers, particularly for earlier assessment years, as it clarifies that the eligibility for tax rebate must be decided based on the provisions of the Income-tax Act and not restricted by administrative circulars or changes in the return filing utility. It also reinforces the principle that a circular cannot take away a benefit that is available under the Act,” she adds.
However, Gupta cautions that taxpayers should note that the position changes from FY 2025-26 onwards, as the Finance Act, 2025 has expressly restricted the Section 87A rebate to tax calculated at the specified slab rates. “Accordingly, the rebate will no longer be available against tax payable on special-rate income, including short-term capital gains under Section 111A,” she concludes.Hence, even though ITAT ruled in favour of the assessee for that particular assessment year, taxpayers should not that this rebate is no longer applicable from this year.

stories.headline: Air India aims for greater synergy with Air India Express to cut costs
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Greater synergy and integration between 
Air India
 and AI Express have emerged as a major way to cut costs, amid spiralling losses. At an Air India board meet here Friday chaired by N Chandrasekaran, the focus was on reducing losses as the AI group has lost over Rs 50,000 crore in just under five years after returning to the Tata fold and the promised capital-intensive revival is a bit distant in the future. Integration of roles at the full service and budget airlines to cut costs, rationalisation of loss-making routes and optimising revenue and fuel efficiency were the key focus areas at the meet. Some important decisions are likely to be conveyed to employees at a town hall that could be convened soon, say sources.
Air India's loss widened to more than Rs 22,000 crore in FY26 due to multiple factors like fuel price rise, rupee depreciation and airspace closure restrictions that make western routes longer. AI's USP is being the only Indian carrier as of now that provides direct connectivity to faraway North America, Europe, Far East and Australia. With western routes affected, this USP can't be capitalised to the hilt.
The board discussed operational and financial matters, to ensure operations are more cost-effective. A significant focus was on increasing fuel efficiency. Air India's new chief executive and MD Tewolde Gebremariam had earlier this month shared his plans for the airline's revival that sees more wide-body aircraft and a battle on costs. 
He feels AI has "punched below its weight" for too long and should "regain market share from competition (foreign airlines)" as that "business belongs to AI."
While the "short term" poses multiple "challenges", the "long term is a huge opportunity" and the deep-in-the-red airline could be profitable "very soon" by focusing on cutting costs and boosting revenue and efficiency.
For this plan, Tewolde sought the board's approval on Friday, a day after the Tata top brass led by Noel Tata and Chandrasekaran visited the airline and aviation academy in Gurgaon.

stories.headline: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
stories.deck: While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output. On the other hand, fuel-related sectors contracted again
stories.bodyText:
Growth in the core industrial sectors of the economy climbed to a series-high of 10.9% in October 2026, driven by a surge in electricity generation, and coal, cement, and iron ore production, and a low base effect, official data released on Friday (November 20, 2026) showed.
Data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on the Index of Core Industries shows that growth in October surpassed the 8.2% in September, the previous series high. The new index, released this year with a base year of 2022-23, has data that goes back only up to April 2024.
However, the data also shows that the strong growth figure in October was also likely aided by the fact that the index grew a relatively poor 0.8% in October last year.
“While core output surged by 10.9% in October 2026, the fastest pace in the new series, this was supported by a low base related to the shift in the festive calendar, with output having expanded by a marginal 0.8% in the year ago month,” Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA said.
“While the growth print for October 2026 signals a strong start for the third quarter of FY2027, this is largely optical,” Ms. Nayar added. “The average performance for October-November 2026 would provide a better assessment, as this would adjust for festive base effects.”
Coal and electricity lead
Within the index, the coal sector saw growth accelerating to 23.05% in October 2026, far faster than the 10.7% registered in September. October’s performance, however, is likely also due to low base effect, since the sector contracted 8.4% in October last year.
The growth in the index, however, is in line with what the industry itself has reported. Coal India, the country’s largest coal company, reported that production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October.
A major reason for the growth in coal production was likely demand from the power sector, which saw electricity generation jump by 21.6% in October 2026, up from 12.6% in the previous month. However, this sector too could have benefited from a low base effect, since it contracted nearly 7% in October 2025.
Infrastructure sectors grow strongly
Within the index, the infrastructure-related sectors were the only ones that grew strongly without the aid of a statistical low base effect.
The iron ore sector, for example, grew at a three-month high of 23.4% in October 2026, compared to 18.4% in September and 8.7% in October last year. One of the factors driving this strong growth was that steel production grew at 7.3% in October, the fastest rate in seven months.
The cement sector also grew at a series-high of 15.4% in October 2026, compared to 10.1% in September, and 5.2% in October last year.
Fuel continues to drag
The fuel-related sectors in the Index other than coal continued to perform relatively poorly.
The crude oil sector saw production contract 4.1% in October 2026, worse than the 1.4% contraction in September and a 0.8% contraction in October last year. The sector has contracted for 22 consecutive months.
Similarly, the natural gas sector contracted by 7.6%, its worst performance in the new series of the index. The sector has contracted for 28 consecutive months.
The refinery products sector saw growth slow to a three-month low of 3.4% in October 2026.
Published - November 20, 2026 06:37 pm IST

briefs.headline: Power & cement fuel October core sector growth of 10.9%
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The core sector grew 10.9% in Oct, driven by strong performance in the electricity, cement, iron ore and coal industries along with a favourable base effect, official data released Friday showed. Sequentially, the growth marked acceleration from an upwardly revised figure of 8.2% in Sept. This is the strongest performance of the core sector in the new series with the revised base year.
During April-Oct, the core sector has grown 6% as compared to 2.3% a year ago. Output in the energy-dominant industries like natural gas (-7.6%), crude oil (-4.1%) and fertilisers (-12.2%) saw continued sequential contraction in Oct, reflecting the impact of the prolonged conflict in West Asia. 
Output in the refinery products (3.4%), though positive, saw sequential deceleration during the month.
Output in the infrastructure-dominant industries such as electricity (21.6%), cement (15.4%), iron ore (26.4%) and steel (7.3%) showed sequential acceleration in Oct, reflecting the divergence in the growth trajectory of energy dominant and infrastructure dominant industries in recent months due to volatile crude prices.
The core sector accounts for 40% weight in the index of industrial production (IIP) and is considered as a precursor of the performance of the country's wider industrial sector.

briefs.headline: Lower tariff: Scotch companies caught in category flipping
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The Scotch lobby may be making noise over tariffs not coming down for bulk whisky despite the India-UK trade agreement, but it is slowly emerging that the Scotch makers industry not only knew about the classification problems but also had got into litigation over the product code used to import at lower duties, which has now come back to haunt them.
While govt officials maintain that India will honour its commitment and they are engaged to find a solution. The problem has its origins in product classification. As part of the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, govt has offered to allow bulk whisky classified as 220830 (six-digit product classification) at 75% tariff, while 220890, which stands for other unadulterated ethyl alcohol, attracts 110% duty. Unlike what the Scotch makers are claiming, no duty concession has been offered to products falling under classification 2106.
Over three decades ago, Bussa Overseas and subsequently Pernod Ricard in 2008 challenged the classification. While Bussa argued that the product should be classified under tariff heading 220810 as it involved the import of bulk concentrates with 60-61% alcoholic strength, given the tariff advantage (this entry was later moved to 210690). 
Customs wanted it classified as finished potable spirits under heading 220830 but lost the case.
With the trade deal in place, and 2106 outside the scope of concessions, the Scotch industry is seeking to flip the product classification from heading 2106 to 220890 - something that they woke up to after negotiators from both sides had finalised the agreement.
"A key concern for our industry is ensuring the inclusion of all our product's relevant tariff codes within the tariff liberalisation schedule. This includes those utilised for the export of bulk whisky products... Tariff code 22089099, which is currently used for the majority of bulk Scotch Whisky exports for regulatory reasons, was not liberalised to the same extent as the Scotch Whisky specific tariff codes, despite industry raising the importance of this," Scotch Whisky Association said in its submission to a parliamentary panel in the UK in Aug 2025.
"As things currently stand, this potentially means a significant proportion of Scotch Whisky exports will not benefit from the agreed tariff liberalisation, undermining the opportunities of this deal for the industry, as well as for the Indian industry which utilises bulk Scotch Whisky, either for bottling in country or as an ingredient in other products. The SWA underscored the importance of these specific inclusions throughout the negotiation process.
 This highlights the need for close, consistent, and meaningful business engagement throughout all stages of negotiations, including access to draft text, in order to avoid such situations from arising," it added.
When caught seeking to reclassify bulk Scotch from 2106 to 220830 to take the tariff advantage, companies and industry bodies representing them sought to blame Indian customs authorities.

briefs.headline: Systematic withdrawal: EPFO seeks income tax tweaks
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
EPFO
 is seeking amendments in the Income Tax Act to ensure that monthly payouts under its newly approved systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) are legally recognised as staged withdrawals, and not as a pension, while also proposing to delink provident fund (PF) membership from traditional employer-employee relationship.
The retirement body wants clarity that periodic installments drawn by retirees - whether drawn monthly, quarterly or annually - are treated solely as a systematic drawdown of their own accumulated savings balance rather than an annuity or pension payout. PF withdrawals at present are structured around final lump-sum settlements upon retirement.
"The matter has been conveyed to the ministry to pursue the matter with the finance ministry. The approval is expected to come soon, with SWP operationalisation kicking soon," a person familiar with the development told TOI. Under SWP, retiring members are being provided with the opportunity to withdraw only a part of their PF corpus and earn interest on the remaining amount. The facility will not be available to members of exempted PF trusts in the initial phase.
In order to enable social security coverage for the vast unorganised workers, EPFO has also proposed breaking the link between PF participation and formal payroll employment. 
Under existing norms, active EPF membership and contributions are tied to an employer-employee relationship. EPFO wants the framework amended so that retired members, platform workers and unorganised sector labourers can continue as active members and contribute independently.
 The retirement fund body has also sought to remove the requirement that PF contributions must originate from "salary". Since gig workers, unorganised labourers and retirees do not earn conventional monthly wages, the amendment will allow them to deposit irregular earnings directly into their Universal Account Number (UAN), while enabling third-party micro-contributions such as incentives or customer tips.
To make solo retirement saving viable where there is no matching employer share, EPFO has requested raising annual contribution limit for self or third-party deposits to Rs 5 lakh, bringing it on a par with the general provident fund threshold for govt employees.

briefs.headline: Anthropic shares plunge 13% a day after debut, retail investors face losses
briefs.bodyText:
Retail investors who rushed to buy Anthropic shares following its initial public offering (IPO) faced losses on Friday as the stock plunged 13%, reversing much of its gains on the first day of trading.
The shares, which opened at $112 on Thursday against an IPO price of $83, closed at $97 before falling to $85 by 12:20 pm ET (1720 GMT) on Friday, according to LSEG data.
The sharp decline came after retail investors recorded more than $750 million in Anthropic share transactions on Thursday, marking the highest turnover for a stock debut in Vanda Research's records. The figure surpassed the $670 million recorded for SpaceX during its IPO in June.
Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece on Thursday in what the report described as the biggest IPO in history, giving public market investors their first opportunity to invest in a leading artificial intelligence company.
The strong retail interest also resulted in the third-largest day of net retail buying for a stock on its debut in records dating back to 2012, according to Vanda Research. However, net buying remained below the records set by SpaceX, at $118 million, and Coinbase, at $92 million.
"Different investors are different but most will be willing to look through the short-term volatility and focus on the bigger future," Viraj Patel, global macro strategist at Vanda, said of Anthropic.
Anthropic said that less than 20% of its shares were allocated to retail investors. A person involved in the offering said the allocation was slightly lower than initially expected because of strong demand from institutional investors.
In the United Kingdom, around 3.6 million shares worth approximately $300 million were allocated to retail investors, according to RetailBook, which coordinated the offering.
British investment platform Hargreaves Lansdown said its clients received 34% of the shares they had requested, in line with allocations made through other platforms.
A European retail investment platform said Anthropic's trading volume, number of traders and average order size on its first day were lower than those recorded for SpaceX.
The decline in Anthropic shares coincided with a broader fall in global stocks on Friday as investor sentiment towards artificial intelligence weakened.
Investors are increasingly seeking stronger returns from the massive investments being made in AI model training, computing infrastructure and data centre expansion.
The concerns have raised questions about whether companies investing heavily in artificial intelligence will be able to generate sufficient returns to justify their expenditure.
Anthropic and SpaceX have reserved a larger share of their IPO offerings for retail investors, with SpaceX allocating around 20% to smaller investors.
Traditionally, IPO allocations have favoured institutional investors, with a 90:10 split between institutional and retail investors, according to Fidelity.

briefs.headline: Noel asks for recordings of Tata Sons meet again
briefs.deck: Trusts Chairman Tells Holdco To Preserve Recordings Of Sept 17 NRC And Board Meet
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Noel Tata on Friday once again sought video recordings of the Sept 17 
Tata Sons
 meetings that culminated in 
N Chandrasekaran
's reappointment as chairman. The company had rejected his demand earlier on grounds that it was not legally required to retain or share recordings of in-person meetings with directors.
The Tata Trusts chairman, who is also a director of Tata Sons, has now asked the company to "preserve" the recordings of both the nomination and remuneration committee (NRC) meeting and the board meeting held that day.
Noel also disputed the minutes of the Sept 17 board meeting and reiterated his position that no resolution on Chandrasekaran's reappointment for a third term had been validly passed as per Tata Sons' articles of association.
While Tata Sons had listed an update from the NRC as an agenda item for the Sept 17 board meeting, Noel maintained that the reappointment resolution was taken up under a "debrief from the NRC". He also contended that the NRC minutes circulated to him were only a draft and did not bear signatures of committee members.
The final minutes of the Sept 17 board meeting will come up for approval at the Tata Sons board's Nov 26 meeting, where directors can either approve them or record their objections.
Noel has also renewed his objection to Tata Sons' filing with the Registrar of Companies on Chandrasekaran's reappointment for another five years under Section 117 of the Companies Act, which mandates that companies file certain board resolutions within a 30-day window.
Noel has also renewed his conflict-of-interest objection over the business relationship between TVS Motor Co, associated with Venu Srinivasan, and Hanno One Warehousing, a company linked to members of N Chandrasekaran's family. Noel's contention is that Srinivasan, a Tata Trusts trustee and Tata Sons director, should have recused himself from the NRC proceedings that considered Chandrasekaran's reappointment. Srinivasan backed the reappointment, with his vote giving Chandrasekaran the support of both a majority of the board and one of the two Trust-nominee directors.
Tata Sons had rejected the conflict-of-interest argument, saying Hanno One has no transactions with Tata Sons or any Tata group entity. It has maintained that a contract awarded by TVS Motor to another company in which Chandrasekaran's family has a disclosed interest does not create a conflict with Tata Sons.

briefs.headline: Record November foreign inflows lift rupee, sensex rises 13%
briefs.deck: Currency Up 4.5% Over Record Low, FPIs Pump In 1.3L Cr This Mth
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Record foreign buying pushed the 
sensex
 up 898 points, or 1.1%, on Friday to 83,920, its highest close in nine months, taking foreign portfolio inflows in Nov past Rs 1.3 lakh crore, an all-time high for monthly flows. FPIs net bought stocks worth Rs 10,308 crore on Friday, 
BSE
 data showed, adding to the Rs 1.2 lakh crore invested till Thursday, according to NSDL data.
The buying lifted the rupee to 92.67 against the dollar, nearly 4.5% above its record low of 96.96 in May. The currency gained around 1.75% this week from 94.3.
Sensex has gained over 9,300 points, or nearly 13%, this month even as global AI-linked stocks came under pressure. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite has fallen over 6% and South Korea's Kospi has declined around 15%. Nifty rose 286 points to close at 25,801. Friday's rally added around Rs 2.2 lakh crore to investor wealth, taking the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies to Rs 514.2 lakh crore, or around $5.5 trillion. Private banks led the gains, with the BSE Bankex and NSE Bank Nifty scaling record highs.
NET FPI flows negative
According to market participants, strong foreign inflows and a shift away from global AI-linked investments supported the rupee. "The rupee witnessed a strong rally, gaining around 0.75% to 92.66... Strong foreign fund flows continue to provide support to the domestic currency," said a market expert, who expects the currency to trade between 92.25 and 93 in the near term.
Foreign exchange reserves, however, fell by more than $14 billion week-on-week to $705.3 billion in the week ended Nov 13, their lowest level in about three months, RBI data released on Friday showed. Foreign currency assets declined by $7.8 billion and gold holdings by $6.1 billion.
According to Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments, foreign investors shifting away from global AI trades supported private banks, while easing concerns over AI disruption helped Indian IT stocks. "Private banks extended their record run as foreign investors... continued to favour the sector's liquidity which are trading at reasonable valuation," he said.

briefs.headline: Why Indian Railways may scrap RAC ticketing system - explained
briefs.deck: Under the existing RAC arrangement, two passengers share a single berth, even though both are charged the full fare. The system has faced criticism over the years, particularly over concerns about passengers paying the full ticket price despite having to share a berth, as well as the inconvenience this causes.
briefs.bodyText:
Indian Railways
’ Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) facility for train passengers may have become redundant with the introduction of digital upgrades to Indian Railways’ ticket-checking system, a section of senior railway officials has argued. The debate comes amid reports that the Railway Ministry is considering discontinuing the facility.
RAC was introduced in 1983-84 by then Railway Minister ABA Ghani Khan Choudhury, who announced the initiative while presenting the Railway Budget in Parliament.
Why was RAC introduced in 1984
Explaining the rationale behind the proposal, Choudhury said a fixed number of berths would be set aside for passengers at the top of the waiting list. This would enable them to receive sleeper berths during the journey if passengers holding confirmed reservations failed to turn up, leaving their berths vacant.
He also maintained that the system had helped prevent railway staff from allotting berths arbitrarily, according to a PTI report.
The Railway Ministry modified the RAC arrangement in 2016 by increasing the number of berths reserved for such passengers. Previously, each sleeper coach had five side-lower berths set aside under RAC, accommodating 10 passengers. The allocation was raised to seven berths, allowing 14 passengers to be accommodated.
The allocation was also increased in air-conditioned coaches. In 3AC, the number of side-lower berths reserved for RAC passengers went up from two to four per coach, increasing the capacity from four to eight passengers. In 2AC coaches, the allocation rose from two berths to three, enabling six passengers to be accommodated instead of four.
Why RAC ticketing may be scrapped
Under the existing RAC arrangement, two passengers share a single berth, even though both are charged the full fare. The system has faced criticism over the years, particularly over concerns about passengers paying the full ticket price despite having to share a berth, as well as the inconvenience this causes.
Officials told PTI that when the reservation and ticketing systems were not digitally linked, RAC was a passenger-friendly initiative. However, digital innovations have changed the scenario.
“If a passenger doesn’t turn up, the train ticket examiner (TTE), who carries a Hand Held Terminal (HHT) that is digitally connected to the entire ticketing system, enters the no-show status against that particular berth, and the same berth becomes available for prospective passengers from the next station,” a senior railway official was quoted as saying.
According to the official, doing away with RAC would also limit the possibility of unfair practices by TTEs by reducing the discretion they currently exercise.
It would require them to finish checking tickets without delay and update the system with the “No Turn-Up” status whenever a passenger fails to board. The vacant berth could then be offered for current booking to passengers boarding at the next station.
The official said the Railways no longer incurs a financial loss when passengers fail to undertake their journeys, following changes to ticket cancellation rules in 2015. Under the revised norms, passengers who do not turn up for their journey forfeit the entire fare paid, without receiving any refund.
“The same berth is then offered to another passenger at the full fare. So, even if the seat goes vacant, there is no financial loss to the Railways because it has already collected the fare from the original passenger,” the official said.
“At the same time, the vacant berth would be offered to other passengers at the next station, ensuring that the facility would not go wasted,” he added.
Railway officials also highlighted a recommendation made by the Parliamentary Public Accounts Committee for a partial refund of fares paid by RAC passengers.
In its report tabled in the Lok Sabha on February 4, 2026, the committee said charging the full fare to RAC ticket holders who remained in the RAC category even after the reservation chart was prepared, without receiving a full berth, could not be justified.
The panel recommended that the Railway Ministry develop a system to refund part of the fare to passengers who paid the full amount when booking but were not allotted an entire berth. Officials, however, said designing such a mechanism would be complicated because tickets are booked through both online e-ticketing platforms and physical reservation counters.
Currently, RAC is not available on Vande Bharat Sleeper trains. Their fares are 30% to 95% higher than those of other trains operating on the same routes.

briefs.headline: Stung by PM Modi's criticism, India Inc fears government may turn cold on tax concessions
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: A day after 
PM Modi
 shellacked India Inc for not translating tax cuts into more jobs and higher salaries, stunned corporate honchos were still trying to process the rebuke, with many worrying the govt may shut the door on any requests for tax concessions.
The "insatiable hunger for concessions" remark by the PM hit members of the industry and businesses at the Ficci event hard. Many sitting in the room only realised the weight of Modi's comment later. Some executives are also seeing it as a signal that govt is in no mood to offer concessions. "It's a signal to back off before the budget," said an industry veteran.
In coming weeks, the industry will be readying data to argue how jobs have increased and wages have gone up.
Executives pointed to the pressure faced by the industry due to increase in fuel and input costs and the impact of a weak rupee that companies had to grapple with until a few weeks ago. However, sources in govt acknowledged the problems but maintained that the industry could have done much more to reciprocate the help govt extended to help them grow and compete internationally. Frustration with the industry's response had been building up.
Officials have argued that from reduction in tax rates, direct as well as 
GST
, to making life easier for businesses, govt had created conditions for the industry to grow at a rapid pace.
Modi's statement is seen as a push to lift real incomes, a key worry for employees and workers since Covid. The 2025 Economic Survey had noted that corporate profitability had soared to a 15-year high in 2024 but growth in employee expense moderated.
In 2023-24, job growth was estimated at 5.6%, while emoluments rose 11.8% with profits rising 10%, according to the Annual Survey of Industries. The latest report showed that persons engaged was up 7.2% to 2.1 crore in 2024-25, and emoluments were up 12.1% to Rs 8 lakh crore. Profits were up 7.7% to 11.6 lakh crore.
Over the past few years, govt and industry have sparred over the pace of investment, with the private sector seen as lagging. In recent months, there has been a pick-up as the impact of lower GST has helped keep consumption strong amid global headwinds.

stories.headline: 50 years later, KL Rahul brings back a rare piece of history in Wellington
stories.deck: KL Rahul achieved a memorable century against New Zealand in Wellington during his first Test innings there. He became the third Indian batter to score a hundred in his debut Test innings in New Zealand. Rahul's century also marked a milestone as the first Indian opener to score centuries in all four SENA countries. This achievement places him among several other renowned Asian batters who have…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
KL Rahul
 added another special chapter to his Test career on Saturday with a memorable century against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.
The 34-year-old became only the third Indian batter to score a hundred in his first Test innings in New Zealand.
He joined Sunil Gavaskar and Surinder Amarnath, who achieved the feat during India's 1976 tour of New Zealand in Auckland. Both scored centuries, with Gavaskar making 116 and Amarnath scoring 124.
Rahul's achievement came 50 years after Gavaskar and Amarnath set the mark. He scored 136 before being dismissed by Nathan Smith.
Rahul completes rare SENA century sweep
Rahul's century also helped him achieve another rare milestone. He became the first Indian opener to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries - South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.
He is now the fifth Indian and eighth Asian batter to achieve this feat. The list includes Mohammad Azharuddin, Sachin Tendulkar, Saeed Anwar, Rahul Dravid, Younis Khan, Kumar Sangakkara and Virat Kohli.
Interestingly, Rahul and former Pakistan opener Saeed Anwar are the only two batters in this group to have scored centuries in all four countries while opening the batting.
Asian batters with Test hundreds in all four SENA countries:
- Mohammad Azharuddin
- Sachin Tendulkar
- Saeed Anwar
- Rahul Dravid
- Younis Khan
- Kumar Sangakkara
- Virat Kohli
- KL Rahul
Rahul joins Gavaskar, Amarnath in elite list
Rahul's unbeaten 124 also made him only the third Indian batter to score a century in his first Test innings in New Zealand.
Indian batters with hundreds in their maiden Test innings in New Zealand:
- Sunil Gavaskar (116) – Auckland, 1976
- Surinder Amarnath (124) – Auckland, 1976
- KL Rahul (124*) – Wellington, 2026
Rahul's century was also the first by an Indian batter in New Zealand in 12 years. Ajinkya Rahane was the last Indian to score a Test hundred in the country, making 118 off 158 balls at the same Wellington ground in February 2014.
Rahul is also the fourth Indian opener to score a Test century in New Zealand. Gavaskar, current India head coach Gautam Gambhir and Shikhar Dhawan are the other three.
Seven countries, seven Test hundreds
With his latest century, Rahul now has Test hundreds in seven different countries. Among Indian batters, only a few have achieved this number of countries, including Mohammad Azharuddin, Sourav Ganguly, Virender Sehwag and Virat Kohli.
Rahul has scored Test centuries in five countries outside Asia. Among Indian batters, only Rahul Dravid has scored hundreds in more non-Asian countries. Dravid has Test centuries in 10 different countries, while Sachin Tendulkar has hundreds in nine.
Rahul among India's leading Test openers
The Wellington hundred was Rahul's 12th Test century as an opener. He is now level with Murali Vijay on the list of most Test hundreds by Indian openers.
Only Sunil Gavaskar (33) and Virender Sehwag (22) have scored more centuries as openers for India.
Rahul has also been among the most consistent Test openers since 2021. He has scored seven hundreds during this period, the joint-most alongside England's Ben Duckett, India's Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sri Lanka's Dimuth Karunaratne.
In the ongoing 2025-27 World Test Championship (WTC) cycle, Rahul has scored four centuries in 21 innings. He is among the leading run-scorers for India in the current cycle and has moved past captain Shubman Gill to become the team's highest run-getter.

stories.headline: 12 vs 9: KL Rahul way ahead of Gautam Gambhir and Rohit Sharma
stories.deck: KL Rahul achieved a significant milestone by scoring his 13th Test century against New Zealand in Wellington. This century places him among India's most successful Test openers in history. He has now scored a total of twelve centuries as an opener, surpassing Gautam Gambhir and Rohit Sharma. Additionally, he has completed the rare feat of scoring centuries in all four SENA countries.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
KL Rahul
 added another milestone to his Test career on Saturday with his 13th century in the format. The right-hander reached the landmark on Day 3 of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.
Rahul completed his hundred with a single off pacer Jacob Duffy. It was his second Test century this year, having scored 100 against Afghanistan at Mullanpur earlier.
With 12 Test centuries as an opener, Rahul is now three ahead of 
Gautam Gambhir
 and 
Rohit Sharma
, who scored nine each.
He is level with Murali Vijay at the third spot on the list, behind only Sunil Gavaskar (33) and Virender Sehwag (22).
Rahul among India's most successful Test openers
Only Sunil Gavaskar and Virender Sehwag have scored more Test hundreds as openers for India than Rahul.
Most Test hundreds as an opener for India
- 33 – Sunil Gavaskar
- 22 – Virender Sehwag
- 12 – Murali Vijay
- 12 – KL Rahul
- 9 – Gautam Gambhir
- 9 – Rohit Sharma
Gavaskar tops the list with 33 centuries, followed by Sehwag with 22. Rahul and Vijay have 12 hundreds each, while Gambhir and Rohit finished with nine apiece as openers.
Rahul among top openers since 2021
Rahul has also been among the most consistent openers in Test cricket since 2021.
He has scored seven centuries during this period, putting him level with England's Ben Duckett, India's Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sri Lanka's Dimuth Karunaratne.
Most Test hundreds as an opener since 2021
- 7 – Ben Duckett
- 7 – Yashasvi Jaiswal
- 7 – Dimuth Karunaratne
- 7 – KL Rahul
He has also been among the leading century-makers in the ongoing 2025-27 World Test Championship (WTC) cycle. 
Rahul, New Zealand captain Tom Latham and Australia's Travis Head have scored four hundreds each as openers, the most in the current cycle.
Rahul achieves rare SENA milestone
Rahul's Wellington century also brought him a special distinction. He became the first Indian opener to score Test hundreds in all four SENA countries - South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.
It was his maiden Test century in New Zealand and his seventh hundred across the four countries.
Rahul is the fifth Indian batter to achieve this feat after Mohammad Azharuddin, Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid and Virat Kohli.
Former Sri Lanka captain Kumar Sangakkara and former Pakistan batters Saeed Anwar and Younis Khan have also scored Test centuries in all four SENA countries.

stories.headline: Countdown: From Steinitz to Gukesh: an elite club of kings
stories.bodyText:
It has been a long time, really.
The first World chess championship was played in 1886. Few sporting events could boast of a longer history.
Yes, the Ashes was already four then. Wimbledon was nine.
After Spencer Gore defeated William Marshall in straight sets to win the title at Wimbledon in 1877, there have been 66 other different champions in the men’s singles. Jannik Sinner, you may recall, became No. 67 four months ago.
The club of the World chess champions is a bit more exclusive. As the event turns 140, there have only been 18 members in that club -- when you consider only the undisputed World champions. (And even if you want to add the disputed ones, the number would go up only by four).
D. Gukesh, and India, will be hoping that the club would have no further addition, at least for the time being. Javokhir Sindarov, however, can be forgiven if he has enough chances to be crowned the new king on the board of 64 squares. The opening move of the World championship match will be played in Geneva on November 24.
Two years ago, Gukesh had become, at 18, the youngest World champion in history when he dethroned Ding Liren in Singapore. Sindarov is only six months older.
The first-ever World champion was a little older, though. Wilhelm Steinitz was 49 when he won the title beating Johannes Zukertort in the match played across three American cities, New York, St. Louis and New Orleans. Steinitz emerged as the champion, winning 10 games to Zukertort’s five. The rule was that the first player to win 10 games would be anointed king of the mind sport. Draws didn’t matter then.
Now they do, and a player has to score 7.5 points in the 14-game match. If it is 7-7, tiebreak games of shorter durations would be employed.
Steinitz defended his title until 1894. He won his match against Mikhail Chigorin (1889 and 1892) and Isidor Gunsberg (1891). Steinitz may have been the first official World champion, but there were brilliant players before him, too. Like Paul Morphy, the original prodigy of chess. The world continues to be in awe of the American who quit competitive chess at 21. Some of the games he played -- like the famous Opera House Game in Paris in 1858, when he took on two men -- continue to fascinate chess buffs.

stories.headline: IND vs NZ, 1st Test: Rahul, Padikkal take India to 239/1 at lunch
stories.bodyText:
K.L. Rahul was at his sublime best, not only completing a milestone but continuing to dictate terms as India closed in on New Zealand’s first-innings total of 368 on the third day of the first Test at Basin Reserve on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
Rahul became the first Indian opener — and only the fifth batter overall — to score a Test hundred in each of the SENA countries. His unbeaten 124 (265b, 9x4, 1x6), alongside Devdutt Padikkal’s 80 (175b, 10x4) and an aggressive Shubman Gill (36 n.o., 4x4), took India to 344 for two at tea, with the second new ball already in play.
Seven runs short of his century at lunch, Rahul had Jacob Duffy resort to a short-ball ploy around the stumps. Consecutive controlled pulls through square-leg fetched him two runs each and took him to 99. He then tapped the ball towards covers and sprinted through for a single before removing his helmet and raising his bat towards the dressing room.
The weekend crowd responded with a rousing applause. The milestone was followed by a reprieve for Padikkal, dropped at gully by Henry Nicholls off Duffy. The duo made New Zealand pay, scoring freely through the rest of the hour, with Rahul continuing to take the lead.
But the second new ball brought an end to Padikkal’s vigil. Kyle Jamieson produced a peach, similar to Akash Deep’s delivery that had breached Glenn Phillips’ defence on Day Two, to beat the left-hander and dislodge his off-stump.
Gill, however, walked in with intent. He stepped out to pull Jamieson through square-leg, attempted an audacious cut off Duffy that resulted in an inside-edge for four, and then followed it up with a perfectly timed cut in the bowler’s next over before finding the boundary with a well-executed pull.
India added 105 runs in 27 overs in the second session, leaving Rahul and Gill well placed to make the most of batting-friendly conditions in the final session and potentially erase New Zealand’s lead before stumps.
